author: M.A. Azad Khokhar
title: For Saeeda, the daughter who gathered his poems
takeaway: A daughter's love turned her father's scattered poems into this book.
scene: This poem is not by Dr. Ahmad. It was written by his close friend, Azad Khokhar, after Dr. Ahmad died. It is addressed to the doctor's daughter, Saeeda Akhtar, a teacher of the Qur'an, who collected her father's poems so they would not be lost. It is the best picture we have of the poet as a person.

original: باپ تیرے دیاں گلاں دھیئے سانوں یاد تے رہنیاں نیں
محفلاں دے وچ اکثر سجناں خشی نشی جو کہیاں نیں
اوہدی فرقت اندر دل نے جگیاں ستاں سہنیاں نیں
پڑھ قرآن آزادؔ جی بخشو نیکیاں جھولی پیاں نیں
transliteration: Baap tere diyaan gallaan dhiye saanu yaad te rehniyaan nain
Mehfilaan de vich aksar sajnaan khushi nashi jo kahiyaan nain
Ohdi furqat andar dil ne jagiyaan sattaan sehniyaan nain
Parh Quran Azad ji bakhsho, nekiyaan jholi paiyaan nain
translation: Daughter, we will always remember your father's words,
the happy things he so often said among friends at our gatherings.
Since he left us, the heart has borne sleepless nights of missing him.
Azad, recite the Qur'an and send its reward to him; his good deeds fill his lap.
couplets.story: Azad tells Saeeda that her father's friends will never forget him. They remember the cheerful things he used to say at their poetry evenings. Since he died, they have spent sleepless nights missing him. All they can do now is recite the Qur'an and pray that its reward reaches him.

original: ہر فن مولا ذات سی اہدی سجن اکثر جان دے سن
پکا پیڈا خدمت جذبہ اوہدے وصف پچھان دے سن
آقا جی دا نعت لکھاری اس تے کرم رحمان دے سن
سجناں دی توقیر تے عزت وچ آزادؔ دھیان دے سن
transliteration: Har fan maula zaat si ohdi, sajan aksar jaan de san
Pakka peeda khidmat jazba ohde vasf pachhaan de san
Aaqa ji da naat likhaari, is te karam Rehmaan de san
Sajnaan di tauqeer te izzat vich Azad dhiaan de san
translation: He was a master of many skills, as his friends well knew;
his steady spirit of service was a quality everyone recognised.
He wrote poems in praise of the Prophet, and God's grace was upon him.
Azad, he always took care to honour and respect his friends.
couplets.story: He was good at many things, and everyone knew it. He loved helping people. He wrote naats, poems praising the Prophet Muhammad, and his friends felt God had blessed him. He always made the people around him feel respected.

original: ملنا جلنا نال محبت ہس دے مٹھے بول دا سی
بھاویں کنی اوکڑ آوے کدی ناں پیروں ڈول دا سی
چاہ پانی خیریت پچھنا حال دلے دا کھول دا سی
گلاں سن آزادؔ اوہ میریاں غم برابر پھول دا سی
transliteration: Milna julna naal mohabbat, has de mitthe bol da si
Bhaaven kinni aukar aave, kadi naa pairon dol da si
Chaah paani khairiyat puchhna, haal dile da khol da si
Gallaan sun Azad oh meriyaan, gham baraabar phol da si
translation: He met people with love, laughing and speaking sweetly.
However hard things got, he never lost his footing.
He'd offer tea, ask how you were, and open his heart.
Azad, he would listen to me and share my sorrow as if it were his own.
couplets.story: He was warm with everyone. He laughed easily and spoke kindly. Even when life got hard, he stayed steady. He would pour you tea, ask how you were really doing, and tell you what was on his own mind. When Azad was sad, the doctor listened and carried that sadness with him.

original: ابو داناں زندہ رہوے دھی نوں سوچاں آئیاں نیں
کیہاں تیرے باپ دے سجناں تدبیراں دوڑائیاں نیں
کیہاں تیرے انھول پنے وچ کیتیاں کجھ چترائیاں نیں
اللہ کرم آزادؔ کمایا محنتاں ثمر لیائیاں نیں
transliteration: Abbu da naa zinda rahve, dhi nu sochaan aaiyaan nain
Kiyaan tere baap de sajnaan tadbeeraan dauraaiyaan nain
Kiyaan tere anbhol pane vich kitiyaan kujh chatraaiyaan nain
Allah karam Azad kamaaya, mehnataan samar liaaiyaan nain
translation: The daughter thought: may my father's name live on.
Your father's friends set plans in motion,
and you, for all your innocence, found clever ways to do it.
By God's grace, Azad, the hard work bore fruit.
couplets.story: After he died, Saeeda wanted to make sure her father's name would not be forgotten. His friends started making plans, and she quietly found smart ways to get things done. With God's help, all that effort paid off.

original: تیری دھیئے بہت اے ہمت جو توں دیوا بالیا اے
شعر پراگا کٹھا کر کے وچ کتاباں ڈھالیا اے
ایس کم دی محنت پاروں جان تے دکھڑا جھالیا اے
دانشمند آزادؔ پے آکھن کم ایہہ کر وکھالیا اے
transliteration: Teri dhiye bahut ae himmat jo toon deeva baaliya ae
Shair paraaga katha kar ke vich kitaabaan dhaaliya ae
Is kam di mehnat paaron jaan te dukhra jhaaliya ae
Daanishmand Azad pe aakhan, kam eh kar vikhaaliya ae
translation: Daughter, it took great courage for you to light this lamp.
You gathered the scattered poems and shaped them into books.
For this labour you bore real hardship.
Azad, the wise now say: she has done it.
couplets.story: Azad tells her it took real courage to do what she did. Her father's poems were scattered everywhere. She gathered them and turned them into books, like lighting a lamp in the dark. It was hard work, and it cost her. Now even the wise people of the town say she achieved it.

original: دھی احمدؔ دی نئیں سعیدہ؟ توں ایں پت جوان آکھاں
دو بدن سی باپ تے بیٹی سانجھی سی اک جان آکھاں
اک کلیاں دی باشنا دیوے دوجا پھل ریحان آکھاں
خوش قسمت آزادؔ اے احمدؔ ہوئی بیٹی ایسی دان آکھاں
transliteration: Dhi Ahmad di naheen Saeeda? Toon ain putt javaan aakhaan
Do badan si baap te beti, saanjhi si ik jaan aakhaan
Ik kaliyaan di baashna deve, dooja phull raihaan aakhaan
Khush qismat Azad ae Ahmad, hoi beti aisi daan aakhaan
translation: Is Saeeda only Ahmad's daughter? I'd say you are a grown son to him.
Father and daughter were two bodies sharing one soul.
One gave off the scent of buds; the other was a basil flower.
Azad, Ahmad was blessed to be given such a daughter.
couplets.story: In their culture people often expected a son to carry on a father's name. Azad says Saeeda did everything a son could have done, and more. She and her father were so close they were like one soul in two bodies. Ahmad was lucky to have her.

original: لوکاں تینوں سن لے دھیئے وانگ کپاہ دے پنجیا اے
ایس کلی دیاں جڑاں مکاؤ کسے ناں پانی سنجیا اے
تیرے حوصلے پست نئیں ہوئے سمیں نوں وا وا گنجیا اے
رب نے مدد آزادؔ ہے کیتی ناں ویلا ہتھوں کھنجیا اے
transliteration: Lokaan tainu sun le dhiye vaang kapaah de pinjiya ae
Is kali diyaan jarraan mukaao, kise naa paani sinjiya ae
Tere hausle past nahin hoe, sameen nu vaa vaa ganjiya ae
Rab ne madad Azad hai keeti, naa vela hatthon khinjiya ae
translation: Listen, daughter: people have pulled you apart like carded cotton.
Some said 'tear this bud out by the roots'; no one watered it.
But your spirit never sank; you stood up to hard times.
Azad, God helped, and the moment was not lost.
couplets.story: Not everyone was kind to her. Some people tore at her the way cotton is pulled apart, and nobody helped her grow. But she never gave up. With God's help, she did not miss her chance.

original: تیرے ابو دی قبر تے اللہ رحمت دا مینہ پاوے جی
چھوٹی موٹی جو وی مشکل سارے دکھ نساوے جی
تیرے دل توں فرقت غم دا مولا بھار ہٹاوے جی
غزل پراگا چھپ کے آوے خشی آزادؔ مناوے جی
transliteration: Tere abbu di qabar te Allah rehmat da meenh paave ji
Chhoti moti jo vi mushkil saare dukh nasaave ji
Tere dil ton furqat gham da Maula bhaar hataave ji
Ghazal paraaga chhap ke aave, khushi Azad manaave ji
translation: May God send a rain of mercy on your father's grave.
May He chase away every trouble, small or large.
May the Lord lift the weight of grief and loss from your heart.
May the ghazal collection be printed, and Azad celebrate.
couplets.story: Azad prays for them both. He asks God to pour mercy on her father's grave like rain. He asks God to take away her troubles and the heavy sadness of losing him. And he prays that the book gets printed, so they can celebrate together.

original: سو کلو میٹر سفر ایہہ کر کے سانگلیوں انکل آیا اے
فون اچانک کر کے دھیئے توں ایہنوں بلوایا اے
کس مسئلے نے تنگ ہے کیتا کس غم خون سکایا اے
تیری ہمت والیاں دھیاں نام آزادؔ کمایا اے
transliteration: Sau kilometer safar eh kar ke Sangliyon uncle aaya ae
Phone achaanak kar ke dhiye toon ehnu bulvaaya ae
Kis masle ne tang hai keeta, kis gham khoon sukaaya ae
Teri himmat vaaliyaan dhiyaan naam Azad kamaaya ae
translation: Uncle has travelled a hundred kilometres from Sangla.
Daughter, you phoned out of the blue and called him here.
What problem was troubling you? What grief had drained you?
Azad, daughters with your courage have made a name for themselves.
couplets.story: One day Saeeda phoned Azad without warning and asked him to come. He drove a hundred kilometres from his town, worried about what was wrong. He ends by saying that daughters as brave as she is earn a name of their own.

original: تیری دکان چ تیری تصویر لگی دعوت دے رہی گل کوئی کر سجن
سمیں ماضی دے اکھاں چ ہوئے حاضر غمی خشی دے ہنجو بھر سجن
ہر میدان وچ تیرا سی پیر اہوندا تینوں نیکیاں لائے سی پر سجن
تیرے وصف آزادؔ پکار اٹھے، محرم حال احمدؔ بندہ نواز سجن
گل صدق خلوص تے ختم ہوندی ہوئے لگن سچی کدے مک دی نئیں
شاخ آس امید دی ہری رہندی پت جھڑ آوے کدے سک دی نئیں
transliteration: Teri dukaan ch teri tasveer lagi daavat de rahi, gall koi kar sajan
Sameen maazi de akhaan ch hoe haazir, ghami khushi de hanjhu bhar sajan
Har maidaan vich tera si pair honda, tainu nekiyaan laae si par sajan
Tere vasf Azad pukaar utthe, mehram-e-haal Ahmad banda-navaaz sajan
Gall sidq khuloos te khatam hondi, hoe lagan sachchi kade mukdi nahin
Shaakh aas umeed di hari rehndi, patt jharr aave kade sukdi nahin
translation: In your shop your picture hangs, as if inviting me: say something, friend.
Past days rise before my eyes, filled with tears of sorrow and joy.
In every field you led the way; good deeds gave you wings, my friend.
Your virtues cry out, Azad: Ahmad understood our hearts, a kind and generous friend.
Every story ends in truth and sincerity; real devotion never runs out.
The branch of hope stays green; autumn may come, but it never dries.
couplets.story: The last part is called 'Dr. Ahmad's picture.' His photo still hangs in his old clinic. When Azad looks at it, it feels like his friend is about to speak. Memories come back, happy and sad, and he cries. Ahmad was always first to do good, as if his kindness gave him wings. He understood people. The poem ends with hope: love that is true never runs out, like a branch that stays green even in autumn.

deeper: The closing lines turn grief into hope. Real love and sincerity, Azad says, never die. That echoes a belief that runs through this whole book: what is done for God and for others with a sincere heart lasts beyond death.
why: Before you read Dr. Ahmad's poems, this one tells you who he was: a warm, generous doctor who loved poetry and the Prophet. It also tells you how the book came to exist. It was his daughter's act of love.
prompt: Whose words or memory would you want to keep alive, and how could you do it?
notes: Stanza 1, line 3: 'jagiyaan sattaan' is read as 'sleepless nights'.
Stanza 7, line 3: 'sameen nu vaa vaa ganjiya' is unclear; it is translated loosely as 'stood up to hard times'.
The last stanza is printed as a six-line musaddas titled 'Dr. Ahmad's picture'. 'Dukaan' (shop) most likely means his clinic.
The stanzas are four-line quatrains, but they use the same 'couplets' field as the rest of the book.
